$comment: Harness config for @vinhnnn/dev-workflow — `bun run doctor` reads `environment`,
Every entry below traces to a real failure mode documented in the README or an ADR.
The `why` on an optional variable is the whole point: without it a newcomer cannot
tell 'this feature is broken' from 'this feature is unconfigured'.

required.name: DATABASE_URL
required.why: there is NO fallback store — without it nobody can sign in at all
required.where: docker compose up -d → postgres on 55432, or a Neon branch

optional.name: PROJECT_ROOTS
optional.why: the filesystem content source finds no repos, so every project reads empty

optional.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
optional.why: the triage analyzer no-ops; ideas can be captured but never analysed

optional.name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
optional.why: `bun run seed` REFUSES to run — it will not put the dev password on a public URL
optional.where: any strong value; set it before seeding a deployed instance

optional.name: GITHUB_TOKEN
optional.why: a deployed instance reads the built-in fixture instead of real repos
optional.where: a fine-grained token with contents:read — read-only since ADR-0010

optional.name: GITHUB_REPOS
optional.why: paired with GITHUB_TOKEN; without it there is nothing to read remotely

blockedCommands.message: Use `bun run test`. Bare `bun test` invokes Bun's own runner, finds ZERO vitest files, and exits 0 — a green result that tested nothing. (Anchored to command starts — begin-of-line, `;`, `&&`, `|` — so a command merely MENTIONING `bun test` in a string still passes; H8.)
Seeding a production database. The seeder refuses without ADMIN_PASSWORD for a reason — stop and confirm with the owner. See __project__/docs/runbook.md.
